Interface conformance checked by hand against campaign/CONTRACTS.md lines 71-81: Checkpointer(path, policy, steps_per_epoch, num_epochs, rewrite_each_epoch=False), .maybe_save(step, epoch, module), .epoch_end(epoch, step, module), .flush(); file keys step/epoch/state; EpochPermutationSampler(n, loader_seed, batch_size, drop_last=True), set_epoch, batch_indices(n, loader_seed, batch_size, step), derive_loader_seed(base, model_seed), seed_for_run = model_seed ^ zlib.crc32(run_id). Also verified: nothing in experiments/, analysis/, tools/ or tests/ imports either module yet (as specified); neither module has any intra-package import, so `import experiments.experiment_code.checkpointing` will not add a dependency cycle; no num_workers/persistent_workers anywhere in generic_scan.py (so batch_sampler + set_epoch in the main process is safe); no pytest filterwarnings config exists, so the sampler's RuntimeWarning will not fail other tracks' tests; no float64/set_default_dtype anywhere in experiments/, so the fp32 checkpoint is bit-exact for this campaign; experiments/nn/nets.py:95 has tie_weights=False by default, so no duplicated tied-weight storage. Two behaviours I confirmed empirically with a throwaway probe script (read-only, no files in the repo):
  base=1234 -> derive_loader_seed = 3732321055; batch_indices(20, 3732321055, 6, 0) = [15,6,3,16,5,0] vs batch_indices(20, 1234, 6, 0) = [3,14,13,2,19,9]  (finding 4)
  "epochs" policy, steps_per_epoch=3, num_epochs=2 -> steps [3, 6], epochs [0, 1]; step 0 absent  (finding 3)

Found no out-of-lane edits: git status shows only the four owned paths as this track's additions.

findings.issue: Lustre hazard: the atomic-write temp name is `f"{path}.tmp.{os.getpid()}"`, qualified by pid only. For a per-run checkpoint that is fine (single writer by design). But `save_init_state` (line 281) writes the *shared* `ckpt/init_mseed{seed}.pt`, and its guard `if not overwrite and os.path.exists(path)` (line 291) is a TOCTOU: at scan start every concurrently launched process for a model seed sees no file and all of them write `init_mseed{seed}.pt.tmp.<pid>` into the same directory. Two processes on different nodes with the same pid (pids are allocated sequentially per node and identically-configured SLURM nodes running the same script cluster in the same range) interleave their torch.save into one temp file, and os.replace then promotes the mangled bytes as the seed's init checkpoint. The same applies to a run checkpoint after a stale-claim takeover (CONTRACTS.md lines 45-49). Nothing detects it: the file is only read back later, by analysis.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the temp name unique per writer, not per pid: `import socket, uuid` and `tmp = f"{path}.tmp.{socket.gethostname()}.{os.getpid()}.{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"`, or use `fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=os.path.basename(path) + ".tmp.")`. One line, removes the whole class of failure.

findings.issue: `flush()` swallows every write failure with a bare `print("  [warn] ...")` and returns None. That is correct for the exception-handler call (it must not mask the exception on its way up), but it is also what happens on the *success* path, where flush runs before the npz, the jsonl and the `done/` marker. A full quota, an EDQUOT, or a Lustre EIO therefore produces a run that is marked `ok` and dedup-skipped forever, with no checkpoint and no trace in any record - discoverable only by grepping stdout of ~16,000 runs. ResNet18 `final` is 45 MB per run and 13 GB per 290-run scan (FABLE_CRITIQUES.md line 137), so hitting quota mid-scan is a realistic outcome, not a theoretical one.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the swallow but make the failure visible to the record: store it (`self.last_error = repr(exc)`) and have the integrator put `ckpt_path` / `ckpt_error` into `record_extra` (schema_version 2); or add `flush(quiet=False)` that re-raises by default and let only the `except`/`finally` call site pass `quiet=True`. State the chosen contract in the integrator notes so analysis can assert every `ok` run has a checkpoint.

findings.issue: Under the `epochs` policy no initial state is recorded anywhere. `maybe_save` returns early unless `policy == "log"`, and `save_init_state` is documented (lines 20-22) and reported as a `final`-policy helper only. Confirmed empirically: policy "epochs", steps_per_epoch=3, num_epochs=2 gives steps [3, 6], epochs [0, 1] - step 0 absent. nanoGPT's C-L3 default is `epochs` and `exp_nanogpt_speedrun` is P0 (CONTRACTS.md line 105), so for the one P0 GPT scan there is no step-0 state in the scan at all: no distance-from-initialisation (the Codex Low 4 item that FABLE_CRITIQUES.md line 140 lists as bought "for free"), no step-0 spectrum for C-L4, and the trajectory starts at the end of epoch 1. The implementer's report defers this ("call save_init_state if nanoGPT needs its init") instead of deciding it, and the integrator has no way to know it must.
findings.suggested_fix: Cheapest correct fix, one line: in `maybe_save`, save step 0 for the `epochs` policy too - `if self.policy == "log" and _is_log_step(step): ... elif self.policy == "epochs" and step == 0: ...` (an extra 3.3 MB per nanoGPT run, negligible against the 115 MB the table already budgets). Otherwise make the integrator note an explicit instruction: call `save_init_state` under `epochs` as well as under `final`.

findings.issue: Silent-wrong-answer trap in the offline reconstruction path. `batch_indices(n, loader_seed, batch_size, step)` expects the *effective* loader seed (the output of `derive_loader_seed`), but per the implementer's own integrator note the run_id - and therefore, presumably, the record - keeps the *base* `_lseed{loader_seed}` so run_ids stay byte-identical. Passing the base produces a different, perfectly plausible batch with no error and no warning. Confirmed: n=20, bs=6, step=0 gives [15,6,3,16,5,0] with the effective seed 3732321055 and [3,14,13,2,19,9] with the base 1234. Both are valid index sets, so a C-L4 Jacobian spectrum computed on the wrong batch has no symptom whatsoever - it just silently answers a different question. Nothing in this track records or exposes the effective seed, and no test covers the base-vs-effective distinction.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a three-line run-level wrapper so the ambiguous call cannot be made by accident: `def batch_indices_for_run(n, base_loader_seed, model_seed, batch_size, step, drop_last=True): return batch_indices(n, derive_loader_seed(base_loader_seed, model_seed), batch_size, step, drop_last)`, and store `base_loader_seed` / `model_seed` on `EpochPermutationSampler` so the runner can record `effective_loader_seed` in `record_extra`. Then promote "the record must carry the effective loader seed" from an aside to a stated requirement in the integrator notes.

findings.issue: The "iterated twice at this epoch" RuntimeWarning will fire as a false positive in the intended wiring. The loops track already passes one loader object as train, test and train_eval loader (tests/test_loops_contract.py:524: `test_loader=loader, train_eval_loader=loader`). With a real EpochPermutationSampler-backed train loader, the per-epoch `train_eval` / test evaluation re-iterates the sampler at the same epoch, so the warning fires once per epoch in every one of ~16,000 runs, and it drowns the one case the guard exists for (a genuinely forgotten `set_epoch`, where every epoch silently replays epoch 0's order - the failure the implementer's note at experiment_utils.py:610/709/781/842 is meant to prevent). Secondary: evaluating the training set through this sampler measures only the drop_last-truncated set, in permuted order, which is not what `train_eval` (index 0 = untrained, CONTRACTS.md line 66) is supposed to mean.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the guard fire on the condition it actually cares about: add `self._epoch_set = False`, set it True in `set_epoch`, and warn in `__iter__` only when `not self._epoch_set and self.epoch == 0 and self._last_iterated == 0`. And add to the integrator notes, as a requirement: `train_eval_loader` must be a separate sequential `DataLoader(train_dataset, batch_size=..., shuffle=False)`, never the train loader object.

findings.issue: Test-file runtime breaks the contract budget (CONTRACTS.md line 19: each file < 60 s). I observed "9 passed in 272.96s (0:04:32)" running it locally on the dev node. Cause: the module-scoped `children` fixture spawns two subprocesses, one per PYTHONHASHSEED, and each exec's sampler.py, which does `import torch` (1-2 min cold on this node per the contract itself). The implementer's reported 6.62 s was a warm-cache batch job, so the number in the report understates it by 40x. Only `epoch_permutation` needs torch; `seed_for_run` and `derive_loader_seed` are pure zlib.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the child: run the crc32 assertions (seed_for_run, derive_loader_seed) in a torch-free child that imports only zlib and re-implements nothing (exec the module with a stubbed torch, or just `python -c "import zlib; print(ms ^ zlib.crc32(rid.encode()))"`), and keep a single torch-importing child for the permutation identity check.

findings.issue: `assert reloaded.load_state_dict(state, strict=True) is not None` is vacuous: `load_state_dict` returns a `_IncompatibleKeys` namedtuple that is never None, so the assertion can never fail. The real guarantee comes from `strict=True` raising, which the assert obscures rather than tests.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop the assert and call `reloaded.load_state_dict(state, strict=True)` plainly, or make it mean something: `incompatible = reloaded.load_state_dict(state, strict=True); assert incompatible.missing_keys == [] and incompatible.unexpected_keys == []`.

findings.issue: The ValueError text in `batch_indices` hardcodes "with drop_last=True" but is raised from a branch that a `drop_last=False` caller can also reach in principle (`per_epoch == 0` is unreachable for drop_last=False, so it is dead but misleading text). Same string is duplicated at line 140 in the constructor.
findings.suggested_fix: Interpolate the flag: `f"no full batch of {batch_size} in {n} examples (drop_last={drop_last})"`, and factor the two copies into one helper or a module constant.

findings.issue: The C-L3 reload acceptance test trains an fp32 model, so the float32 downcast in `cpu_fp32_state` is a no-op there and the 1e-6 tolerance is really being exercised as bit-exactness - the tolerance the module docstring (lines 16-17) justifies by the fp32 storage is never actually needed. It also compares val and *train* losses, where C-L3's test text says "validation and test losses". Harmless for this campaign (I grepped experiments/ and there is no float64 or set_default_dtype anywhere, so every run is fp32), but the test would not catch a regression if a future toy/polynomial run is switched to fp64.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add the fp64-model variant to the existing parametrisation of test 1 (train the fp64 model, reload the fp32 state into a fresh fp64 model, assert < 1e-6) - the fp64 path is already built in `test_state_is_a_cpu_float32_clone_including_buffers` - or add a one-line comment saying the tolerance is slack for a future fp64 run and the campaign is fp32 today.
